Summary:
You have a moderate risk for kidney problems. This means your body may be under some stress, especially because your waist is 107 cm and your hemoglobin is 12 g/dL. These numbers can point to extra body fat or possible changes in how your blood works, so it's important to stay on top of your health.

Food habits:
Since your waist is large, it's a good idea to choose foods that help reduce belly fat. Eat more vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins like chicken, fish, or beans. Limit processed foods and sugary drinks. Since your hemoglobin is normal, you don't need to worry about anemia, but staying well-nourished helps your body work better. Talk to a doctor or dietitian if you want a plan that fits your lifestyle.

Rest and sleep:
Try to get 7 to 9 hours of sleep each night. Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day. Good sleep helps keep your blood pressure and blood sugar steady, which supports your kidneys.

Daily routine:
Move your body a little every day. Try walking 20 to 30 minutes most days - even around the block or on a flat path. This helps with weight and keeps your heart and kidneys working well. Stay active, but don't push yourself too hard. You can do this slowly and safely.

Follow-up reminder:
Because your risk is moderate, it's important to check with your doctor soon. Ask for a urine test to check for protein (called UACR) and a blood test to check your kidney function. These tests can help find early changes. Don't wait - talk to your doctor in the next few months to confirm your risk and get a plan.
